summary: B's dataset is structurally identical to A's failure mode — possibly worse. All 500 cases fall into exactly 25 templates of 20 cases each. Within each template cluster, every case shares: title (often LITERALLY identical), intrinsic_quality, signal, season_pattern, human_factors, expected_signal_summary, expected_outcome, expected_status, human_judgment, edge_case_flag, AND the entire events_timeline narrative except the final 'Month N: X likes Y reports' line. In ~13 of 25 clusters even the like/report numbers are 100% identical across all 20 cases. The only varying fields are usually duration_months, final month label, type rotation, and (in some clusters) location_desc — but ~14 of 25 clusters use generic non-specific location_desc ('Random track in Tararuas', 'Standard track mark', 'Various NZ track', 'Average NZ track', 'Tourist viewpoint', 'Backcountry hut, various', 'Native bush viewpoint, location varies', etc.) which independently fails criterion 3. Clusters 861-880 (silent majority) and parts of 941-960 (cairn) also have events_timeline of only 2 lines, violating the min-4 rule without qualifying exception. The top-30 list contains the cluster-leading cases that have specific real NZ locations (Aoraki Hooker, Routeburn, Copland, Mueller, Ball Pass, Cascade Saddle, Gillespie, Olivine, Garden of Eden, Whitcombe, Tongariro, Taranaki, Whanganui, Mueller/Sealy, Whataroa) — but even these are still part of clones for the algorithm's purposes. Quality score: 2/10. This dataset is not usable for algorithm testing without major rework: B clearly used a small set of hand-written templates and mass-cloned them into ~20 instances each, exactly the failure mode the user described in A. Recommend rejection of this batch.
